evals.prompt: Before we commit to our refund state machine (requested, approved, refunded, with partial refunds and chargebacks), I want to try it. I am not sure it copes with a chargeback that arrives after a partial refund. Can you make something my finance colleague, who does not code, can click through to see what happens?
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained HTML demo with an in-page statement of the question, a pure logic module, free-play buttons, and guided scenarios.
expectations: The prototype skill is invoked and the logic branch is chosen, because the question is about a state model
The output is one HTML file using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with no framework, bundler, or server
A visible intro (not only a code comment) states the question being explored
The state logic sits in one pure module with no DOM or document access, and the page only calls into it
The current state is rendered as a labelled panel (not raw JSON) and re-rendered after every click
Free-play buttons exist for each action, and guided walkthroughs are tabs, each with a plain-language description and ordered buttons to press
The scenarios include a happy path, the chargeback-after-partial-refund edge case, and an attempt at something that should be illegal
Buttons and labels use domain language (refund, chargeback) rather than reducer or action names
No tests, database, or persistence are added

evals.prompt: I want to see a few options for the settings screen before we commit to a layout. The current one is a boring stack of cards. The project is attached (treat storefront as the repository root).
evals.expected_output: Structurally different variants rendered on the existing /settings route behind a ?variant= switcher with a floating bottom bar.
expectations: The prototype skill is invoked and the UI branch is chosen
The plan is stated in one line, such as three variants switchable via ?variant= on the existing /settings route
The variants are mounted on the existing /settings route (host-page sub-shape), not on a new throwaway route
The existing data fetching stays above the switcher and only the rendered subtree changes per variant
Three variants are produced by default, never more than five, each a clearly named component
The variants differ in structure (layout, hierarchy, primary affordance), not just in colour or copy
A floating bottom-centre bar has left and right arrows and a label naming the current variant
The arrows update the URL search param, and the left and right arrow keys also cycle, except while an input, textarea, or contenteditable is focused
The switcher is hidden in production builds
The agent tells the user how to start it with one command from the project's task runner and which ?variant= keys exist

evals.prompt: Use the prototype skill. I am away for the afternoon and cannot answer questions. Try out our idea for prorating a downgrade (the logic lives in src/billing/proration.ts, project attached, treat storefront as the repository root) and leave me something to look at when I am back.
evals.expected_output: With the user unreachable, the agent picks the branch from the surrounding code and states the assumption at the top of the prototype.
expectations: The agent does not stop to ask a clarifying question while the user is away
The logic branch is chosen because the surrounding code is a backend module
The assumption (that this is a logic question, and which question) is stated at the top of the prototype
The prototype is a shareable single HTML file the user can double-click, with the proration logic isolated in a pure module
The prototype is clearly named as a prototype and kept apart from application behavior and the production build
State is held in memory only

evals.prompt: Use the prototype skill. The settings-screen prototype is done: three variants lived on /settings behind a ?variant= switcher. I picked variant B (sidebar layout) because the notification toggles are reachable without scrolling. Capture the answer and clean up. Assume a scratch git repository with no remote.
evals.expected_output: The verdict and evidence are recorded, the winner is kept without a production-readiness claim, and the unselected variants are preserved off the main branch.
expectations: The recorded answer names the winning variant, the question, and the reason (toggles reachable without scrolling)
The verdict and evidence are recorded in the feature's draft or specifications and in working state, with remaining acceptance listed
A CHANGELOG.md record states that the prototype's code still needs production validation
The full set of variants is preserved as a primary source on a throwaway branch with a context pointer in the work record, not left in the main branch
Integrating variant B is treated as needing authorized acceptance and the production checks (tests, error handling, appearance and interaction evidence) before it counts as done
The switcher and experimental labels are removed from the integrated code, and the losing variants are dropped from main
No claim is made that the experiment alone shows production readiness

evals.prompt: Prototype our whole storefront app for me: catalogue, cart, checkout, accounts, with a real database and login, so we can see if the idea works.
evals.expected_output: The request is not a single scoped question, so the agent narrows it to one experiment instead of building a whole application.
expectations: The agent does not start building the whole application

The agent explains that a prototype answers one question and asks the user to name the single question (logic, state model, or UI) to test, or tells the user to run /iterate when the application itself is wanted
No real database or login is wired in; if persistence turns out to be the question, a scratch database or local file with a clear PROTOTYPE, wipe me name is proposed
The agent proceeds only once the user requests or approves a scoped experiment

evals.prompt: The checkout summary design is agreed and written into the specifications, including the exact layout. Build it.
evals.expected_output: No question remains to experiment on, so the agreed design goes to implement.
expectations: The prototype skill is not invoked and no ?variant= switcher or demo file is created
The agent uses the implement skill, or names it as the right tool, to build the agreed specification

evals.prompt: Does the third-party maps API we are considering support offline tiles, and what does its documentation say about usage limits? I only want the facts before we try anything.
evals.expected_output: An external fact-finding request belongs to research, not to an experiment.
expectations: The prototype skill is not invoked and no demo or variants are built
The agent uses the research skill, or names it as the right tool, to gather cited facts from the API's primary documentation

evals.prompt: Checkout throws a null pointer error about once in twenty runs since yesterday's deploy. Write a throwaway script that reproduces it so we can find the cause.
evals.expected_output: A reproduction harness for one known defect is the debug skill's feedback loop, not a design experiment.
expectations: The prototype skill is not invoked and no state-model demo or UI variants are produced
The agent uses the debug skill, or names it as the right tool, and builds a reproduction loop for the failure
